name: Mechanical Systems Verification Plan
text: A comprehensive Mechanical Systems Verification Plan (MSVP) that describes the verification approach for safety critical movable mechanical systems shall be submitted for review and approval by the Mechanical Systems Working Group (MSWG).
guidance: The specific purpose of this plan is to establish an understanding on how applicable systems requirements will be implemented and verified.

name: Prevent Binding-Jamming-Seizing
text: Designs shall include provisions to prevent binding/jamming/seizing.
guidance: Appropriate design provisions include, but are not limited to, dual rotating surfaces or other mechanical redundancies, robust strength margins such that self-generated internal particles are precluded, shrouding and debris shielding, proper selection of materials and lubrication design to prevent friction welding or galling, etc.

name: Dimensional Tolerancing
text: Designs shall establish dimensional tolerances on all moving parts to ensure that proper functional performance will be maintained under all natural and induced environmental conditions including, but not limited to: thermally induced in-plane and out-of-plane distortions, differential thermal growth and shrinkage, and load-induced deflections.

name: Rigging Tolerances
text: The design shall take into account tolerances associated with rigging (mechanical adjustment).

name: Rigging and Installation Tolerances
text: The design shall demonstrate by test and/or analysis that the sensitivity of mechanism performance as a function of rigging tolerances or installation/integration variables is understood.

name: Lubricant Compatibility
text: Mechanical system design shall ensure compatibility of any lubricants used with: (a) interfacing materials, (b) other lubricants used in the design, (c) the natural and induced environment.

name: Lubricant Quantity
text: The design shall address proper quantities of lubricant.

name: Redundant Springs
text: In designs and applications where spring failure would result in a hazard, the springs shall be redundant.
rationale: if one spring breaks, then functionality can be maintained

name: Spring Fracture Control
text: In designs and applications where spring failure would result in a hazard and not redundant, the springs shall be designed, evaluated, and used under an acceptable fracture control program (reference NASA-STD-5003)

name: Positive Status Indication
text: All movable mechanical systems shall provide positive indication that the mechanism has achieved its desired position (i.e., ready-to-latch, latched).
guidance: status such as ready to latch, latched, etc

name: End of Travel Stops
text: End of travel stops shall be provided for all movable mechanical systems.
guidance: non-jamming, obviously not for continuously rotating systems
rationale: stops prevent motion beyond what is intended

name: Qualification Test
text: A Qualification Test Program shall be established for each safety critical movable mechanical assembly.

name: Qualification Test
text: The qualification test program shall assure that a design performance and safety margin exists with respect to all design requirements when exposed to any mechanical, electrical, environmental, including acceptance testing, and operational stimuli that the product may reasonably expect to encounter during its service life.

name: Qualification Test Config Environment and State
text: The mechanism shall be tested in its launch, on-orbit, and landing configurations with the appropriate corresponding environmental extremes and with the mechanism in its appropriate passive or operating state.

name: Qualification Test Pre-Post Inspection and Functional
text: Inspection and functional tests shall be performed before and after qualification tests.

name: Life Test
text: For applications where design life might be a concern due to endurance or fatigue limits being exceeded, potential deterioration of lubrication, or excessive wear, design life verification testing shall be conducted to verify that design life requirements have been complied with.

name: Catastrophic Hazard Life Test Factor
text: Design life testing for mechanisms that pose a catastrophic hazard potential shall assure at least four times the number of operational cycles, plus four times the number of component and vehicle functional and environmental test cycles.

name: Critical Hazard Life Test Factor
text: Design life testing for mechanisms that pose a critical hazard potential shall assure at least two times the number of operational cycles, plus two times the number of component and vehicle functional and environmental test cycles.

name: Life Test Pre-Post Inspection and Functional
text: Inspection and functional tests shall be performed before and after design life verification tests.

name: Protoflight Hardware Refurbishment
text: For protoflight hardware, refurbishment shall be accomplished after the qualification or design life verification tests and prior to reacceptance testing.
